metadata.note: Predecessor railroads added in response to a question about when Utica, NY got passenger rail: Aug 1 1836, via the Utica and Schenectady Railroad, connecting at Schenectady with the already-running Mohawk and Hudson Railroad (1831, one of the first railroads in the US) for through Albany-Utica service. Syracuse followed in 1839. Ten such connecting roads along the Albany-Buffalo corridor were consolidated in 1853 to form the original New York Central Railroad -- well before Vanderbilt's 1869 Lake Shore acquisition that the pre-existing 'Water Level Route (Albany-Chicago)' feature in this file starts from. Geometry for these four predecessor features reuses the relevant Albany-anchored prefix of that same feature's detailed GTFS-derived alignment (since the Water Level Route has always run this same natural Mohawk Valley corridor), rather than new hand-drawn waypoints.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utica_and_Schenectady_Railroad (incorporated Apr 29 1833, opened Aug 1 1836; freight barred until 1844 to protect the parallel Erie Canal; connected with the Mohawk and Hudson at Schenectady, and gained a westbound connection Aug 3 1839 via the Syracuse and Utica Railroad; consolidated with nine other railroads in 1853 to form the first New York Central Railroad, led by Erastus Corning)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact opening date/year for the Mohawk and Hudson Railroad's Albany-Schenectady segment beyond '1831' (commonly cited but not verified to the day here); precise frequency for any predecessor era, all estimated; names of all ten railroads in the 1853 consolidation beyond the two discussed here.

Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
